html:
On 16 March 1988, Iraqi planes dropped chemical weapons on the Kurdish town of Halabja in northeastern Iraq, near the Iranian border. Between 3,000 and 5,000 people were killed, most of them civilians, and thousands more were injured.

It came near the end of the Iran-Iraq War, after Iranian forces and Kurdish fighters had taken the town. The gases, likely mustard gas and nerve agents, killed families in the streets and in their cellars. It was part of the Anfal campaign, in which the government of Saddam Hussein killed tens of thousands of Kurds and destroyed thousands of villages.

The West, then leaning toward Iraq, said little at first. Iraqi courts later called it genocide. One of the commanders, Ali Hassan al-Majid, called Chemical Ali, was hanged in 2010.
sum: On 16 March 1988, Iraqi planes dropped chemical weapons on the Kurdish town of Halabja in northeastern Iraq, near the Iranian border. Between 3,000 and 5,000 people were killed, most of them civilians, and thousands more were injured.
